children: The Central Bank of the Republic of Azerbaijan kept its discount rate unchanged at 6.5% for a fourth consecutive meeting on September 23, 2026, maintaining borrowing costs at the lowest level since September 2021.
However, the lower bound of its interest rate corridor was cut by 0.5 percentage points to 5%, while the upper bound remained at 7.5%.
The move widened the corridor to encourage interbank trading amid excess liquidity, while keeping the key rate and upper bound unchanged to stabilize inflation expectations.
Annual inflation eased to 5.7% in August from 5.8% in July, remaining within the target range, while core inflation stood at 5.1%.
Foreign currency supply continued to exceed demand, helping reserves rise 32.9% to a record $15.3 billion in the first eight months of 2026.

The bank maintained that global energy and food prices remain key upside risks to inflation, while future decisions will depend on inflation, foreign exchange market conditions, and banking liquidity.

title: Azerbaijan Holds Key Rate at 6.5%, Widens Rate Corridor
